title: Cross-device Latency Prober and Attention Kernel Swapper for Prefill/Decode Coordination
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
Teams are observing tail latency and cost regressions on heterogeneous multi-GPU racks during mixed prefill+decode workloads. Current kernel selection is static per model variant and the NCCL overlap heuristics assume steady-state throughput; both assumptions break down when sequence length distribution and token arrival patterns vary across requests.

Goal:
Design and implement a low-overhead cross-device latency prober plus an in-flight attention-kernel swap mechanism that: (1) measures per-stage latency and NCCL overlap slack online, (2) dynamically switches to attention kernels (and related memory layouts) better suited to the observed sequence length / KV cache hit pattern, and (3) coordinates a lightweight staggered prefill/decode handoff to maximise NCCL overlap without introducing jitter for short-lived requests.

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end 95th percentile latency reduction for mixed workloads on 8xA100 and 4xH100 racks by >= 12% vs baseline (runtime-1.18).
- Token throughput (tokens/sec) change within +/-3% or improved relative to baseline for typical batch sizes.
- No increase in error rates or OOM-caused falls back beyond current levels.
- Feature can be toggled per-customer and per-cluster with safe rollback in <5 minutes.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Cross-device latency prober:
   - Microprobe threads launch very small, representative microbatches (1-4 requests) on a configurable cadence (default 1 probe per 30s per GPU group).
   - Each probe collects: kernel execution time per attention op, NCCL allreduce/allgather durations, memcpy times, and KV-cache hit/miss counters.
   - Probes are marked low-priority and isolated to spare compute windows using nice-levels / CUDA stream priorities to avoid perturbing production traffic.

2) Dynamic attention-kernel swapper:
   - Maintain a compact runtime profile per model variant: {seq_len_bucket, kv_hit_rate_bucket, preferred_kernel_id}.
   - On detecting a sustained shift (configurable smoothing window, default 120s) in the profile, atomically switch kernel selection policy for new requests on that model variant.
   - Kernel switch points: choose boundaries that preserve compatibility (same numerical precision / quantization path); if incompatible, fall back to a compatible variant with a seamless redirect.

3) Prefill/Decode handoff steward:
   - Implement a staggered handoff policy where prefill microbatches release NCCL windows in microtime-slices to allow decode stages to start earlier without saturating inter-GPU links.
   - Use probe-derived NCCL slack metric to increase or decrease slice widths.

Instrumentation & telemetry:
- New metrics: probe_latency_ms (per-stage), nccl_slack_ratio, kernel_switch_count, probe_influence_impact_ms, kv_hit_rate_by_bucket.
- Logs: structured events for kernel_swap decisions including before/after profiles and triggered probes.
- Dashboards: per-cluster heatmaps for nccl_slack_ratio and kernel efficacy.

Safety and rollout strategy:
- Default to disabled. Enable via runtime flag per-cluster and per-model.
- Start with internal-only clusters (dev, perf), then canary to a small % of production traffic on non-critical customers.
- Monitor 5m rolling error/tail-latency; auto-rollback if 5xx or 95p latency increases by >10% for 10 consecutive minutes.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (spike, 2w): probe prototype that measures kernel and NCCL timing in isolation (bench-only mode).
- M2 (engine, 3w): integrate probes into serving runtime as low-priority asynchronous tasks and record metrics to TSDB.
- M3 (scheduler, 3w): implement kernel selection policy store and atomic swap API for model variants.
- M4 (handoff, 2w): staggered prefill/decode steward and config knobs for slice sizing.
- M5 (canary+hardening, 2w): dashboards, safety monitors, and rollout tooling.

Risks & mitigations:
- Probe perturbation: use stream priorities and rate-limit probes; validate on perf clusters before enabling in prod.
- Kernel incompatibility: only allow swaps inside compatible kernel families; require per-model validation tests.
- Oscillation (flip-flop) of kernel choices: use hysteresis (min dwell time 120s) and exponential backoff for switch attempts.
- NCCL saturation misprediction: fall back to conservative slice widths if error rates increase.

Next steps (this ticket scope):
- Complete M1 prototype and a short write-up of probe design choices.
- Attach microbench results and a basic dashboard mock for nccl_slack_ratio.

- Initial perf spreadsheets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-Perf-Probes
- Spike branch (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1439
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95p latency reduction >= 12% on mixed workloads vs runtime-1.18; 2) Tokens/sec within +/-3% of baseline; 3) No OOM regression; 4) Runtime flag toggles and rollback <5 minutes
design_notes:
- Use CUDA stream priorities and cpu-side nice to make probes minimally invasive.
- Kernel IDs are small integers persisted in the runtime config store (consistent read across nodes).
- Sequence length bucketing: [<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024].
- KV hit rate buckets: [0-25%, 26-60%, 61-100%].
- Hysteresis: require a 3-sample majority over a 120s sliding window to trigger swaps.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe instrumentation; integration tests that simulate probe cadence and validate no more than 1% added latency; perf tests on 8xA100 and 4xH100 racks using synthetic mixed seq_len workloads; chaos test that injects artificial NCCL delays and validate rollback triggers.
deployment_plan: Feature gated via runtime flag + per-cluster feature bit. Canary rollout: internal perf cluster -> 2 non-critical production customers (1% traffic) -> 10% traffic -> full. Monitor metrics for 24h at each step.
benchmarks: Spike bench (dev cluster): baseline 95p=1120ms, probe-enabled 95p=970ms (13.4% drop) on mixed-traffic synthetic; tokens/sec change -0.8%. Results in PR 1439 comments.

2025-03-02 - Nora Kim (perf): Ran 10-hour mixed workload experiments. 95p improved by ~11-14% depending on rack topology; H100 racks show larger gain. Added heatmap to dashboard mock.
2025-03-04 - Security Review (automated): flagged kernel swapper for review due to config store access. Added requirement for audit log entries on swaps.
2025-03-05 - Diego Alvarez: Pushed atomic swap API prototype. Preparing M2 PR for integration and TSDB instrumentation. Next: add auto-rollback hooks and extend dashboard.
Notes: Be cautious about naming parity with existing 'rendezvous' and 'conductor' components — this feature should be surfaced as 'prober + swapper' in UI to avoid confusion.
